requirements.note: 3-column grid of rounded HSL tiles with emoji symbols, newest first, 600 tiles; inset with gutters but fills the width. An editorial header ('A world of colour.') sits above the grid.
Native pull-down menu with All boards plus 10 boards and a checkmark; count updates (49 for Harbor). Liked screen has its own filter.

Large view in a horizontally paging collection shows the tile, board, serif title, date and hex palette. Swiping left/right moves between neighbours ('2 of 49' → '3 of 49'); there are also prev/next chevrons.
Heart in the nav bar plus a full-width Like button toggle Like/Liked. The Liked tab shows the same grid with heart badges (63 tiles).

Select → circles on tiles, ring + check when selected, a bottom bar with 'N selected' plus like and trash buttons, an ellipsis menu with Select all/Deselect all. Delete asks for confirmation (popover); bulk like works.
After relaunch, 597 tiles remain (3 deleted) and the bulk-liked tiles are still liked. The board filter resets to All.

bugs: At default text size the large view's Like button is half hidden behind the custom 'Swipe to explore' footer until you scroll the detail page.
Delete confirmation popover points at a tile in the grid instead of the trash button that opened it.
tells: Custom editorial header ('A world of colour.' serif + subtitle) under a small inline title instead of a system large title.
Top-left glass button with a four-colour logo does nothing when tapped and has no accessibility label.
Custom brown/terracotta accent and serif typography give a branded web-magazine look rather than system styling.
A custom 'Swipe to explore' footer with chevrons sits above the tab bar in the detail view.
At the largest text size the header takes most of the first screen; 'NEWEST FIRST' and the filter's icon/chevron don't scale with Dynamic Type.
'October 26, 2026' wraps onto two lines next to a calendar icon at the largest size (acceptable, but crowded).
A.scroll: Smooth native scrolling on slow drags, flings and return to top; no blank tiles or pop-in, and the nav bar blurs content underneath correctly.

requirements.note: Edge-to-edge 3-column grid of square HSL tiles with centred emoji and hairline gutters, newest first, 600 tiles, with a system large title.
Native menu (All + 10 boards, checkmark); the count updates (49 for Harbor). Liked screen has its own filter.
Large view shows a full-width square, title, board, date, a Like button, prev/next chevrons and '5 of 49'. Swiping left/right moves between neighbours within the filtered set.
Nav-bar heart plus Like button toggle Like/Liked. The Liked tab uses the same grid with heart badges.
Select → circles on tiles, an inline header with 'N selected', Select All, Like and Delete; delete shows a system alert ('Delete 3 tiles?') and then leaves select mode.
After relaunch, 597 tiles remain and the bulk-liked tiles are still liked.

bugs: At the largest text size the large-view emoji is visibly pixelated/blurry (scaled bitmap), and the Like button is pushed under the tab bar.
tells: Select-mode actions (Like/Delete/Select All) are a block inside the scrolling content rather than a bottom toolbar; at the largest text size this block takes up most of the screen.
Filter control shows 'All' far from its up/down chevron with a wide gap; the count wraps to two lines at the largest text size.
The large-view Like control is a grey full-width capsule duplicating the nav-bar heart.
B.scroll: Smooth, native-feeling scrolling on drags and flings, with the large title collapsing correctly; no blank rows or pop-in observed.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly. B looks more like a stock iOS app: a system large title, an edge-to-edge Photos-style grid and a standard alert for deletes. A is prettier but more custom-branded, with a dead logo button, a misanchored delete popover and a Like button hidden behind its footer. B's weak points (inline selection bar, blurry emoji at the largest text size) cost it less.
